dimensions.assessment: Affects specific National Park Service lessees, commercial operators, and administrative personnel involved in park lease management.
Enables high-value redevelopments exceeding $100,000,000 and lease terms up to 99 years, creating major localized commercial effects.
dimensions.evidence: redevelopment costs of which are expected to exceed $100,000,000

dimensions.assessment: Involves private capital investments in park properties exceeding $100 million, but does not explicitly appropriate federal funds.
Amends lease administration authorities under title 36 of the Code of Federal Regulations and mandates regulatory revisions.
dimensions.evidence: revise part 18 of title 36, Code of Federal Regulations, to reflect the authority granted

dimensions.assessment: Permits lease extensions and long-term leases spanning up to 99 years, establishing lasting administrative changes.
dimensions.evidence: lease term of not more than 99 years

missing_information: Exact number of current leases eligible for extension under this authority
Total projected federal administrative cost for processing these lease agreements
importance_detail.rationale: The bill authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to extend certain National Park System leases without competitive bidding and to enter into long-term leases of up to 99 years for redevelopments exceeding $100 million. While individual lease agreements may involve substantial financial investments, the overall systemic reach is limited to specific park concessionaires and properties meeting high cost thresholds.
